name: Khao
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired Glottolog bookkeeping entry; 'Khao' is an exonym for Kháng (khan1274); only old vocabularies (Bouchet 1935/1936, Macey 1906)

sources.note: No sentence on stress or accent; summarizes Tạ 2021 (8 tones, Ci(Cm)V(Cf)T template, monosyllables dominate). Reference list supplied the record for Tạ Quang Tùng 2023 (Vietnamese book).

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2010. The Kháng language of Vietnam in comparison to Ksingmul (Xinh-mun). In McElhanon & Reesink (eds.), A Mosaic of languages and cultures, 138-154. SIL e-Books 19. Than Uyên (Lai Châu) variety.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Kháng-specific stress statement. Generic remark that Mon-Khmer word shapes are weak-syllable (reduced vocalic and prosodic features) + strong-syllable (p. 139); Kháng 'possesses word structure that shows only vestiges of the original sesquisyllabic pattern' and has six tones (p. 144); §2.1 lists sesquisyllabic animal names with reduced classifier ʔbu. (p. 145); §3 'Kháng has word structure that is very similar to Tai languages', six tones with trajectories plotted (pp. 149-150). p. 144: 'the Kháng in Thuận-châu are called Xá Khao or White Kha' (identity of khao1244).

sources.citation: Tạ Quang Tùng. 2021. A Phonology and Lexicon of Khang in Vietnam. JSEALS 14.2: i-xxix. hdl:10524/52487 (CC-BY). Nam Mu village, Tuần Giáo district, Điện Biên variety.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: the words stress/accent/prominence do not occur. Describes Khang as 99.45% monosyllabic, template (C1ə̌/ǎ).C2(C3)V(C4)T with only 5/917 sesquisyllabic words whose presyllables have reduced vowels /ă, ə̌/ (p. iii); 8 tones (6 live-syllable, 2 dead-syllable) plus modal/creaky/glottal register (pp. viii-xi). Notes Mikami (2003) found Thuận Châu Khang strictly monosyllabic C(C)V(C)/T with 4 tonemes (p. ii).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page khao1244 'Khao' (retired bookkeeping entry; refs Bouchet 1935/1936, Macey 1906, Proschan 1996, Edmondson 2010, Eberhard et al. 2025).
sources.note: No linguistic content. Justification: Khao is 'an exonym used mainly in older sources' for 'a fraction of the Kháng in Thuan-Chau, but the language is the same'; consolidated with Kháng [kjm].

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 registration authority page for code xao 'Khao' (https://iso639-3.sil.org/code/xao).
sources.note: No linguistic content; the code xao is still listed as Active (individual, living) in ISO 639-3 even though Glottolog has retired khao1244.

sources.citation: Tạ Quang Tùng. 2023. Ngữ âm tiếng Kháng và phương án chữ viết cho người Kháng ở Việt Nam. Thái Nguyên: Nhà xuất bản Đại học Thái Nguyên.

sources.note: Book-length Vietnamese phonology of Kháng by the author of the 2021 JSEALS description; most likely to contain an explicit statement on trọng âm (stress) vs thanh điệu (tone) and would supersede the 2021 article.

sources.note: The only phonological description of the Thuận Châu (Sơn La) Kháng, i.e. exactly the population called Xá Khao/Khao (xao); 42-page phonology with wordlist may carry a prosody/stress remark; Tạ 2021 reports it gives strictly monosyllabic C(C)V(C)/T with four tonemes.
